title: Virtual screening identifies antiplasmodial beta-haematin inhibitor chemotypes
summary: Molecular docking and Bayesian/SVM classifiers screened a ChemDiv 300k library. Researchers tested prioritized commercial compounds and reported coumarin and iminodipyridinopyrimidine chemotypes active against beta-haematin and whole-cell P. falciparum, including chloroquine-resistant parasites. This is one bounded in-vitro campaign, not clinical evidence.
ai_technology: Bayesian and support-vector classifiers; molecular docking

evidence.tested: Primary abstract reports prioritized compounds with beta-haematin and whole-cell parasite activity.
evidence.unknown: A 2023 conference abstract may disclose an early coumarin result; the article’s specific two-chemotype campaign is retained without priority claim; no clinical evidence.
evidence.ai_role: Sequential ligand/structure virtual screening prioritizes commercial compounds for biochemical and parasite assays.

source_review.scope: PMC-hosted primary full article; PubMed primary record/abstract. Material checked for the specific claims stated in the record.
